div.head: High Priority Species of Greatest Conservation Need
div.p: Table A1-2 includes all HPSGCN in the 2025 SWAP. HPSGCN may be listed as endangered, threatened, or special concern in New York, be habitat specialists, or have a restricted range in the state. The status of these species is known, they have an established breeding, wintering, or migratory population in New York, and they have experienced a population decline in New York. These species have identified threats that may put them in jeopardy, and they require timely management intervention to reverse or slow population declines and lead to recovery. Without the implementation of conservation actions over the next 10 years, they are likely to reach critically low population levels in New York.

div.head: Species of Greatest Conservation Need
div.p: Table A1-3 includes all SGCN in the 2025 SWAP. SGCN may be listed as special concern in New York, or not currently state listed. The status of these species may either be known, and they have an established breeding, wintering, or migratory population in New York; or the status may be poorly understood, but they are suspected to have a breeding, wintering, or migratory population in New York. These species may have experienced historic population declines that are now stabilizing or on a positive trajectory; they may be declining or beginning to experience declines in the state; or there are features of their life history that make them particularly vulnerable to threats. There are one or more identified threats to these species, and there is uncertainty regarding their longterm viability or persistence in New York. These species would either benefit from the implementation of conservation actions to maintain stable population levels or sustain recovery in New York; or research is needed to determine their actual status, trends, or specific management actions that could lead to maintenance of their populations in New York.
